title: Stop Making TUIs: AI Agents Make Native UIs Almost Free
description: Simon Willison highlights Thomas Ptacek's argument that developers should build real native user interfaces even for small personal tools because 'coding agents have reduced the cost of getting a usable-enough GUI up and running to almost nothing.' Willison notes he hasn't yet habitually built native UIs for all projects but is 'running out of excuses.' The shift represents how AI-assisted development is changing default patterns for tool creation.
author: Simon Willison

title: LLM 0.32.1 and OpenRouter Plugin with Server-Side Tools
description: Simon Willison released LLM 0.32.1 fixing a dependency issue with OpenAI's Python library dropping httpx, and llm-openrouter 0.7 adding compatibility with LLM 0.32. The OpenRouter plugin now displays reasoning traces and adds three new server-side tools: Shell, WebFetch, and WebSearch. These tools can be enabled with options like `-T WebSearch`, allowing LLMs to execute shell commands and perform web searches during conversations.
author: Simon Willison

title: Hacker News: Launch HN - Bullet (YC S26) - A Faster Coding Agent
description: Y Combinator S26 startup launch for Bullet, claiming to be 'a faster coding agent.' The launch post and discussion reflect the competitive landscape of AI coding tools in 2026, with numerous startups pursuing similar goals of faster, more reliable code generation. Comments examine technical claims, benchmark comparisons, and the differentiation strategies in a crowded market.
author: Hacker News Community

title: ArXiv Research Activity: 3,667 CS Submissions in August 2026
description: ArXiv reports significant research activity with 3,667 recent Computer Science submissions as of August 20, 2026, and 3,577 entries in the Artificial Intelligence category (cs.AI) for August 2026. On August 21, 2026 alone, there were 222 new submissions. Total arXiv submissions across all categories reached 3,140,535. Submissions typically post Sunday through Thursday with a 2:00 PM Eastern deadline for same-day 8:00 PM publication.
author: ArXiv

title: Andrej Karpathy: End of 'The Era of Typing Computer Code'
description: Andrej Karpathy reports that programming underwent a dramatic transformation in December 2025, marking the end of 'the era of typing computer code into an editor.' Before December, coding agents 'basically didn't work,' but since then models have gained 'significantly higher quality, long-term coherence and tenacity,' completing complex multi-step tasks that previously took entire weekends. Karpathy describes an agent independently setting up SSH keys, installing vLLM, benchmarking models, creating endpoints, building a web UI, testing everything, and generating documentation—all within 30 minutes. The emerging discipline involves 'ascending the layers of abstraction to set up long-running orchestrator' systems managing multiple parallel coding instances.
author: Andrej Karpathy

title: ChatGPT Search Now Uses Site:Operator at Scale
description: Simon Willison reports on Promptwatch data showing ChatGPT search underwent a major change around August 8, 2026, with the percentage of search queries containing the site: operator jumping from 0.3-0.5% to 16-17%. This corresponds to OpenAI's August 6th announcement about updating GPT-5.6 Sol for more reliable facts. The data suggests ChatGPT's search tool has a shape like `search(query, recency, domains)` rather than encouraging the site: operator directly. Additionally, ChatGPT appeared to greatly reduce the likelihood of Reddit being used in searches starting August 18th.
author: Simon Willison

title: Hacker News: 2x, Not 10x - Coding with LLMs in 2026
description: Discussion emphasizing realistic productivity gains from AI coding tools, with developers reporting 2x improvements rather than the hyped 10x claims. The conversation focuses on sustainable productivity improvements, the learning curve for effective AI coding workflows, and the gap between marketing promises and actual developer experience. Participants share practical experiences measuring productivity gains.
author: Hacker News Community

title: Hacker News: Why Write Code in 2026?
description: Hacker News discussion explores treating 'coding agents as the new compilers' and how this mindset 'gives us permission to ship terribly written code.' Commenters debate whether agents are truly like compilers or something fundamentally different. The discussion reveals evolving attitudes about code quality, trust in AI-generated code, and the philosophical implications of treating AI output as equivalent to compiled machine code.
author: Hacker News Community

title: SmolVM as Sandbox for Untrusted Python & JavaScript
description: Simon Willison documented research into using smolmachines.com's smolvm as a secure sandbox for running untrusted Python and JavaScript code with RAM and CPU time limits, no network access, and restricted filesystem access. When the Claude Code for web environment couldn't run smolvm due to lack of nested virtualization support, the AI agent creatively solved the problem by running tests in GitHub Actions runners which do expose /dev/kvm. Willison notes this is 'another example of Fable being relentlessly proactive.'
author: Simon Willison

title: Warp Factories: Out-of-the-Box Software Factory for AI Development
description: TechCrunch reports on Warp's introduction of 'Warp Factories,' a new infrastructure system designed as an 'out-of-the-box software factory for AI development.' The platform aims to streamline the creation of AI software factories and reduce complexity in AI development, allowing teams to deploy AI coding capabilities without building foundational infrastructure from scratch. This represents a broader trend toward standardized tools for AI development workflows.
author: TechCrunch

title: AI News of the Week: Beyond Demos into Questions of Trust
description: Weekly AI news summary (August 11-18, 2026) highlighting a major industry shift: AI is moving beyond impressive demonstrations into questions of trust, ownership, infrastructure, and profit. Key developments include OpenAI's breakthrough analog AI chip, new workplace AI learning systems reading more like humans, drone training systems with virtual rewards, and machine learning pipelines for artistic recognition. Generative AI has reached 53% population-level adoption in just three years.
author: Industry Analysis

title: Anyone Can Write Code Now, So What Gets You Hired?
description: Super Data Science Podcast Episode 1019 (August 18, 2026) with Priyanka Vergadia. Episode addresses how AI coding assistants have lowered barriers to entry for programming, forcing employers to shift focus toward higher-value competencies that AI cannot easily replicate. Discussion covers differentiating skills beyond pure code generation including problem-solving, system design capabilities, communication and collaboration abilities, understanding business context, adaptability and learning aptitude, and architectural thinking.
author: Super Data Science Podcast with Priyanka Vergadia

title: Hacker News: Coding Agents Have Replaced Every Framework I Used
description: Hacker News discussion on how AI coding agents have changed the economics of building custom tooling, with developers reporting that agents can 'de-slopify code,' check for code smells, and identify scalability problems. The conversation reflects on how the default approach to framework selection and tool building has shifted in 2026, with AI agents making custom solutions more viable than off-the-shelf frameworks.
author: Hacker News Community

title: Qwen 3.8 27B Scores 52 on Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index
description: Simon Willison notes that Qwen 3.8 27B scored 52 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, matching GPT-5.6 Luna (max) and just one point behind GLM-5.2 (max) and DeepSeek V4 Pro 0813 (max). Willison calls this 'truly astonishing' given that the competing models are 753B, 1.7T, and unknown parameters, while Qwen 3.8 achieves this at just 27B parameters.
author: Simon Willison

title: Amazon AI Training Facility Scanning Books for Training Data
description: Simon Willison covers 404 Media's investigative report tracking rare book shipments with AirTags, revealing they ended at an Amazon AI training facility in Las Vegas. The VGT3 corner of the LAS8 Amazon facility features a logo of 'a dinosaur with a book,' and online forum discussions between Amazon workers confirmed that VGT3 'destructively scans large volumes of books.' This follows previous reports of book dealers receiving large orders from price-insensitive anonymous customers suspected to be scanning books for AI training.
author: Simon Willison

title: Hacker News: Ask HN - Best Option for Hosted Agent in 2026?
description: Community discussion seeking recommendations for hosted AI agent solutions in 2026. Commenters compare options including OpenClaw, Claude Agent SDK, and various hosted solutions. The discussion reveals the fragmented state of AI agent infrastructure, with developers weighing trade-offs between different hosting approaches, API providers, and agent orchestration frameworks.
author: Hacker News Community

title: Qwen 3.8 27B: Excellent but Wildly Overthinking by Default
description: Simon Willison provides an extensive review of Qwen 3.8 27B, an Apache 2 licensed 27B parameter vision-capable LLM from Alibaba's Qwen research lab. While calling the model 'excellent,' Willison documents how it 'defaults to wildly overthinking things' with excessive reasoning traces. The review includes detailed examples, performance analysis, and comparisons with other models. Willison notes 27B is 'an excellent size for running a model on a reasonably specced laptop.'
author: Simon Willison

title: CORS Chat: Web UI for OpenAI-Responses-Compatible Endpoints
description: Simon Willison built CORS Chat, a web UI for exercising OpenAI-Responses-compatible chat endpoints, to help test Qwen 3.8 27B running in LM Studio. The tool provides conversation persistence in the browser with JSON export, and includes the feature of progressively rendering SVG images while tokens are still streaming in. Willison tested it against LM Studio with the `--cors` option and OpenRouter.
author: Simon Willison
